title: Sharpening a fixed fs monoid chart and its characteristic stalks
statement:
Let $(U,M,\alpha)$ be a locally Noetherian fs log scheme and $Q\to\Gamma(U,M)$ a global chart by a fine saturated monoid [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Put $S(Q)=(\operatorname{Spec}_{\mathrm{mon}}Q,\overline{\widetilde Q})$, the sharpened monoid spectrum [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. For $u\in U$ set $E_u=\{q\in Q:\alpha(q)\in\mathcal O_{U,u}^{\times}\}$. The rule $u\mapsto Q\setminus E_u$ and the chart homomorphism induce a local morphism of sharp monoidal spaces
$$c_Q:(U,\overline M)\longrightarrow S(Q).$$
The log structure $M$ is associated to a log structure on the Zariski site, and $c_Q^{-1}\overline{\widetilde Q}\to\overline M$ is an isomorphism of Zariski sheaves. Here $\overline M$ is the quotient of that Zariski log structure by $\mathcal O_U^\times$. For every geometric point $\bar u$ over $u$, its comparison map canonically identifies both characteristic stalks with $Q_{E_u}/E_u^{\mathrm{gp}}$, where $Q_{E_u}=Q-E_u$ inside $Q^{\mathrm{gp}}$. These comparisons commute with restriction to open subsets of $U$. Every stalk of $S(Q)$ is saturated and has torsion-free group completion.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.1.2--3.1.10, pp.98--100; 3.3.2--3.3.4(ii), p.107; 3.3.12, p.108: sharpening a fixed fs monoid chart.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-chart-characteristic-stalk-comparison] to obtain Z,e,z,a,b with association, chart and section compatibility, the normalized numerator formula, and the ordinary/geometric comparison on every local log-section germ.

Apply [lem-trf-chart-characteristic-fan-map] to the resulting Zariski chart and its normalized ordinary stalk equivalences. This gives f with the required point formula, bijective stalk maps, and numerator formula. Each bijective monoid homomorphism has a multiplicative inverse, so it is local. Apply a_x to an invertible target-stalk element: an invertible Associates class is one, and injectivity gives sharpness.

For any open W, its inclusion preserves the neighborhood colimit: the image-on-neighborhoods functor is left adjoint to inverse image, so its opposite is final. Its canonical colimit isomorphism is inverse to the actual FineFan.stalkMap of the open restriction, as checked on each neighborhood coprojection. Compose its inverse with a_x to define aW. The inverse identity gives the required equation on all stalk elements. Substitute the already obtained ordinary/geometric comparison to prove the restricted equation for every local section.

For every prime p of Q, its complement F is a submonoid and a face, since the ideal absorbs products and 1 is excluded by properness. Its closure is F itself. Use [lem-trf-affine-fan-localization-sections] to identify the actual affine stalk with Associates(Q_F), and [lem-trf-fs-face-sharpening] to obtain saturation and a finite integral basis for its completion. The equivalence induces the canonical equivalence on group completions. Transport saturation of the monoid range across it. The basis makes the completion torsion-free over the integers, so a positive power equal to 1 forces the element to be 1. This applies to every prime, independently of the scheme image.

proof_origin.place: Stage 3 C9: original Steps 1 and 3 split as chart-characteristic-stalk-comparison; Steps 4 and 5 split as chart-characteristic-fan-map. Locality, sharpness, open-restriction compatibility and all-prime saturation/torsion-freeness are proved in Lean from these and the original face and affine-stalk dependencies.

This is a first split, not a re-split: live and side-live hold the item unsplit with an identical statement. The item statement matches 3.1.8 + 3.3.2 + 3.3.12, and all cited nodes are in unit sk-i-curve-zero. Steps 2-6 check out: E_u is a face, so Q minus E_u is a prime ideal. fs-face-sharpening and affine-fan-localization-sections give Q_F/F^gp as the stalk at every prime, including the empty prime. The explicit inverse maps of step 3 are well defined because Q is integral, and they kill E^gp. The unit loci V_a are open, the localization map on the basis is well defined because the sections of M-bar are sharp, the stalk isomorphisms are local, and restriction to opens is compatible. The new node (sheafified Zariski logification, its change to the étale site, pushout stalks, restriction compatibility) is true. Kato's construction checks out on Spec k with N, with beta(1) zero or a unit, and with the identity on O_X. It overlaps the étale-site nodes prelog-pushout-log-axiom, prelog-pushout-hom-extension and etale-log-presentation-comparison only in its étale clauses, so it is not a duplicate and does not restate the item. Searches are recorded and there is no SGA. FIX (C3/E5): step 1 identified L_E with M by lem-trf-associated-log-universal-stalks, but that lemma concerns the constant-presheaf construction L_X(Q,beta). I added the bridge: ε^{-1} is left adjoint to ε_*, constant-sheaf sheafification, and U is final, so maps from ε^{-1} of the constant sheaf Q are the same as maps Q -> K(U). L_E and M then have the same universal property and are canonically isomorphic. I added uses def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, lem-trf-commutative-monoid-sheafification and def-trf-geometric-morphism and synced proof_deps. The statement is unchanged.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
